title: Viewport continuity and legacy-browser harmonization for console surfaces (tables, charts, modals)
creator: Aria Chen
description: Goal: ensure consistent viewport behavior and graceful feature degradation across modern and legacy enterprise browsers for three high-traffic console surfaces: resource tables, time-series charts, and modal flows. We need a design + implementation approach that keeps the console visually stable and usable at narrow widths (320px) through large desktop (1920px), while avoiding large polyfills that increase bundle size. Scope: - Define breakpoints and continuity rules for tables, charts, and modals. - Provide CSS and interaction fallbacks for browsers that lack sticky positioning, IntersectionObserver, CSS grid subgrid, or high-DPI canvas scaling. - Create documented design tokens and component variants for legacy-fallback styles (overflow-safe tables, simplified chart rendering, and stacked modal layout). Out of scope: full IE11 feature parity; we will provide graceful degradation and a documented list of unsupported behaviors for end-users on severely outdated browsers. Acceptance criteria: - Tables: sticky header behavior preserved or replaced by visual affordance (row separators + persistent header row) without horizontal overflow on 320px widths. - Charts: canvas-based charts render at correct devicePixelRatio across Safari/Firefox/Chromium; fallback to SVG or simplified bar rendering on legacy browsers. - Modals: focus-trap and scroll-lock work on iOS Safari and Edge Legacy; modal stacking/order preserved, no body scroll bleed. - No regressions in Storybook visual snapshots for the three surfaces across Chromium 120, Safari 16, and Firefox 115. - Design handoff assets in Figma and a developer playbook in Confluence linked below. Implementation constraints/decisions: - Prefer CSS feature queries (@supports) and progressive enhancement. - Use small targeted JS fallbacks (IntersectionObserver polyfill only where strictly necessary). - Avoid including a generic polyfill bundle; keep total added bundle < 8KB minzipped. - Use Playwright cross-browser tests instead of adding heavy screenshot-only tooling to keep CI fast. Links: - Figma prototype: https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE/console-viewport-continuity - Confluence doc (detailed spec & playbook): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/UX/pages/Console+Viewport+Continuity - Example GH PR for sticky-table fallback (implementation spike): https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/12345
comments: 2025-02-13 - Aria Chen: Initial design spike uploaded to Figma. Prototype includes an alternate stacked row layout and a compact chart rendering mode. Seeking engineering input on feasible chart fallbacks for WebGL-less environments.

2025-02-18 - Mateo Ruiz: Eng review — prefer canvas with devicePixelRatio scaling for primary charts; fallback to simplified SVG bar/line for older browsers. Suggested IntersectionObserver polyfill only for table virtualization. Marked estimate to 5 points.

2025-02-22 - Priya Anand (PM): We should prioritize the billing cost view and rollout dashboard first since customers repeatedly reported layout shifts in those pages. Reordered implementation backlog accordingly.

2025-02-25 - Eng (frontend): Implementation note — Safari 15 on iOS has an issue with position:sticky inside transformed parents. Proposed fix is to avoid transforms on container wrappers for pages with sticky headers and rely on sticky fallback class that switches to 'position:relative' with an anchored header.

2025-02-27 - Accessibility review (external consultant): Modal focus trapping approach is fine, but keyboard-only users need a visible focus outline in the compact table variant. Added focus-visible token requirement to tokens checklist.
2025-03-01 - Design QA (Aria): Visual QA run against Playwright snapshots completed. Found a 1px header misalignment in Firefox for large-font settings; created ENG-8950 to track pixel alignment fix.

2025-03-03 - Mateo Ruiz: In Review — changed chart fallback to use inline SVG for small sparkline variants to make keyboard and screen-reader annotations easier. Documented trade-off: SVG fallback increases DOM nodes but greatly improves accessibility.
2025-03-03 - Aria Chen: Updated Figma with accessible tokens and added compact-table variant for mobile. Preparing final dev handoff package.
